Welcome Home

by AnodeAntarcSkywalker

Summary

“Is it ready?”

“Almost,” March said, stretching her hand out and summoning various crystal shards. The floor lit up in a soft purple glow, the outline resembling the symbol of Fuli. The Remembrance. Opposite to her, Caelus had out his quill, poised to write something. Herta was clutching her key tightly, her fourth mirror floating beside her.

Phainon nodded, steeling his resolve. The other Heirs were standing at the sidelines, watching with fascination as the light grew brighter and brighter. This was it, he told himself. This was the day he was waiting for for so long. 

The Dome of the Stars seemed to glow brighter than ever, like they knew what was going to happen right now. They were glittering in the colors of her, in those beautiful shades of purple, pink, teal, blue and baby yellow. 

The one who helped bring forth the true dawn, yet never got a chance to witness it herself. The daughter of Aedes Elysiae. The original bearer of the Coreflame of Time. Khaslana and Phainon’s best friend.

It was time to bring her back.

“Is it ready?”

“Almost,” March said, stretching her hand out and summoning various crystal shards. The floor lit up in a soft purple glow, the outline resembling the symbol of Fuli. The Remembrance. Opposite to her, Caelus had out his quill, poised to write something. Herta was clutching her key tightly, her fourth mirror floating beside her.

Phainon nodded, steeling his resolve. The other Heirs were standing at the sidelines, watching with fascination as the light grew brighter and brighter. This was it, he told himself. This was the day he was waiting for for so long. 

The Dome of the Stars seemed to glow brighter than ever, like they knew what was going to happen right now. They were glittering in the colors of her, in those beautiful shades of purple, pink, teal, blue and baby yellow. 

The one who helped bring forth the true dawn, yet never got a chance to witness it herself. The daughter of Aedes Elysiae. The original bearer of the Coreflame of Time. Khaslana and Phainon’s best friend.

It was time to bring her back.

Herta stepped forward, inspecting the circle and asked Fourth Mirror to do a quick scan. She nodded in satisfaction when the lighter buzzed green. “Well done both of you,” she said airily, not looking at March and Caelus. “Most of your work is done. I can take it from here.” She sighed. “If only Screwy were here right about now…”

She let out another sigh and faced Phainon. “Listen up, World Bearer,” she started to say in a stern tone, any hint of lightness gone from her voice. “I'm going to say this only once, so you better keep your ears open. We've only got one shot of getting your friend out of the loop before the causality loop breaks.”

Phainon nodded once again, not trusting his voice. He knew this. He knew why Cyrene couldn't make it with them after Caelus had explained everything that happened after the final battle. As the Demiurge–the literal heart of the world, she had to seal herself away once again in the hidden corner of time after interfering in the 33,550,336th cycle. To ensure Amphoreus’s survival, and to guarantee Iron Tomb's permanent downfall. It was a sacrifice that broke him for a few days. 

Caelus shot him a sympathetic look, which he returned with a weak smile. They know. They all know.

Herta continued speaking. “Now that the little one here has collected enough memory juice, and with March being a pure child of Anasrava, we have what we need to restore the whole planet. However, before that, we need to bring Cyrene back. Ultimately, in the end it'll be you, her and Caelus to be the ones to bring Amphoreus to the cosmos. She was–is the heart of your home after all.”

Anaxa stepped forward and cleared his throat. “I understand that Phainon would be the best candidate to traverse through the memoria, but aren’t you more experienced in memories? I heard it was thanks to you and your companion you were able to breach the Scepter and reach out to the Nameless, and you were able to warp the memoria tides for a while. Naturally, in that case, wouldn’t you be the better person to go instead?”

“Good points, but also the wrong ones,” Herta said, folding her arms. “It’s true I know my way around memories despite being Nous’ Emanator, but I’m not Genius. There’s a reason why I walk the path of Erudition, not Remembrance. And before you say Phainon is on the path of Destruction, it’s because the Destruction and Remembrance are so intertwined with each other, instead of repelling each other they somehow work in harmony.”

“It’s a unique phenomenon,” Fourth Mirror chimed in all excited. “Usually, the Destruction is a path that, obviously, destroys whatever in its path without question. And naturally, as you may expect, THEIR Pathstriders follow the same. Except for dear old Mr. Phainon here. His Destruction was to preserve your home, and keep everything intact, while Ms. Cyrene handled the memories part.”

It turned to glance at Phainon. “When you two started the Recurrences, your paths slowly started to intertwine with each other, and slowly because of your actions, the Destruction and the Remembrance were, to put it bluntly, indistinguishable. You two became the flip sides of the same coin. You always walked forward, while Cyrene was in the past, nurturing the Demiurge Core until it bloomed. Love and hate.”

“I wouldn’t say indistinguishable,” said Herta, now smirking. “But I was thoroughly surprised by the data the Little One gave me. And thanks to that, only I know how to properly conduct this experiment. If I go in and you all mess up, who knows what will happen? Plus, I’ve only spoken to Cyrene once, but–”

She faced Phainon, her face softening ever so slightly that it surprised him a little. “I know you two were close. Therefore, you are everyone’s only hope. I’m sure you can bring her back from her prison. And once you do, I can use all your memories to reseal Amphoreus’ causality, and you and Cyrene can use your Emanator powers and remake the planet how you see fit. And before anyone asks, no need to worry, you won’t have to do this alone.”

“Understood,” Phainon said, wincing at how raspy his voice came out. Right, his voicebox was going to take some time for it to fully heal. He cleared his throat. “How long must I take?”

“As long as you need, though I do prefer you not take literal days,” Herta quipped. “The sooner we finish this the better, and I’m a busy woman. The Space Station needs my immediate attention after this.”

Caelus raised a brow. “I thought Asta had everything under control. Did something happen?”

Herta shot him a withered look. “My Space Station still suffers from the virus Iron Tomb unleashed, even though you and Cyrene purified the cosmos from it. The systems weren’t exactly saved, and only I have the proper access codes. Now then Little One, do your magic. March, keep the flow as steady as you can, and make sure nothing but the memory of your brief encounter with Cyrene is the only thing in your mind.”

“Got it,” March nodded, raising her hand again and closing her eyes. A harsh, mauve light hit Phainon’s eyes as it grew in size, causing him to squeeze his eyes shut. So did the other Heirs and Caelus save Herta, who let out a satisfied hum. The light got brighter and brighter, swallowing his vision–

Until after two minutes it didn't.

And then Phainon opened his eyes and his legs nearly gave way.

Standing before them, without a trace of life was Cyrene herself. Demiurge. How he also imagined Cyrene would look like if she actually had a chance to grow up. The only time was all the way back in cycle zero, and even then her appearance hadn't changed, like a certain administrator willed for it. 

Her multicolored eyes were staring blankly up ahead, her pristine long dress unnaturally stiff. Even her long pink hair didn't have its usual lustre to it. Phainon couldn't stop the violent shiver that went down his spine. Mydei caught his eye and gave him a reassuring look.

Herta stepped forward and inspected every angle, making sure every minute detail was present. Of course it'd be, March’s work was always flawless. Give her any task that involves memories now and she'd be able to do it. Caelus mentioned it was scary at first, while Dan Heng found it fascinating. 

“Good work,” she finally said, eyes filled with satisfaction. “Of course I'd expect nothing less from a pure child of Anasrava. Better than those garden folk. Now,” she whipped around and pointed her key staff at Caelus, “it's your turn. And you,” she faced Phainon, “If you want to say goodbye to your friends, do it now. We won't know how long it'll take you to reach where Cyrene is, and time is going to flow differently. Better not leave behind any regrets.”

Herta turned around, giving him some privacy which he was much thankful for and jogged over to where his fellow Heirs were standing, all looking at him with sad smiles. 

“So this is it,” Tribbie said, voice low and cracking as she fretfully wiped her tears. “This is goodbye then, isn't it?”

“For now.” Phainon crouched down to her level. “This isn't like all the other farewells in the past Tribbie. I'll return home soon enough with Cyrene.”

“I really want to meet her again,” chimed Hyacine. Little Ica bobbed her little head up and down. “It's been long since I had a proper tea party with Reney.”

Anaxa nodded in agreement. “The very first Nouspore. I'd love to have a talk with her.”

“Just don't overwhelm her Anaxagoras,” Aglaea said, rolling her eyes before kneeling and placing a hand on Phainon’s cheek. “I know you can do it Phainon. Stay safe no matter what, and bring the final member of this family home.”

“Oh, and do me a favor and bring whatever goodies might be there,” Cipher purred, tail swishing back and forth. “Even if it’s just a small coin, I don’t mind.”

“Cipher!” Castorice exclaimed, punching her arm and rolling his eyes. “Ignore her Lord Phainon, you know how she gets. We both wish you a successful journey,” she added politely, her arms folded across her skirt.

“Me and Dux Gladiorum both give you our blessing, Dux Solaris,” said Cerydra, her staff in hand. Hysilens nodded, not speaking anything, but the comforting look on her face spoke volumes.

March sauntered over to where Dan Heng was standing and smiled brightly. “You’ve got this Phainon!” she said cheerfully, eyes crinkling. “Go bring your friend and my sister back, and once Amphoreus is a real planet, we’ll throw a huge party!"

“Maybe not immediately,” Dan Heng sighed. “But we will all be waiting for your safe return, no matter how long that may take.”

Phainon felt someone tug at his coat and was immediately tackled into a hug by the triplets, landing on his back and let out a sharp laugh as they nuzzled their heads against his chest, wrapping his hands around all three of their frames. 

“Be safe Snowy,” Trianne mumbled, pinpricks of tears forming at the corner of her eyes, which Phainon wiped off with his thumbs. “Please bring little Reney home. We miss her so much.”

“We will pray for both of you,” added Trinnon. “We know that if anyone can go back in time and save Little Reney, it's you Snowy.”

The three jumped off him, fluttering their little bronze wings and said in unison, “So, let the West Wind grant you safe passage and guide you to your destination!”

Phainon laughed wetly, giving the trio one last hug before turning to the final person, who walked over and punched him in the arm.

“Ouch!” he said in mock pain, rubbing the spot. “What was that for?”

“No reason,” Mydei shrugged. “Everyone gave you words or encouragement, I just did what I always do before you set off on a journey. Don’t tell me you’ve forgotten.”

“Couse I haven’t,” he chuckled, returning the favor. “But at least back then we’d have a rough idea of how long each mission would take. Now though…it’s better not to leave behind any regrets, right?”

“Mmm…” And then the king pulled him for a quick hug, patting his back and whispered, “Don’t lose yourself, alright? You’ve been doing so well the past months. Just remember that we’ll all be here, waiting for your return.”

“I know.” They pulled apart. “I promise I'll be OK. I'll go, get her out and we'll be back in a jiffy. Besides, something tells me I'm going to need her help to come back anyway. I can't wait for you to meet her.”

Mydei nodded. “Now go, Boy Saviour. Don't keep her waiting. I'll be right here, waiting for your glorious return.”

Right on cue Snowy padded up to him, giving him a ferocious yip. He hopped into Phainon’s open arms and nuzzled his cheek with his nose, yipping again.

“Don't worry buddy,” he said, gently patting his head. “You’ll see her soon. And once she’s back we’ll play the games we used to play.”

Snowy yipped one last time, wagging his tail and licked his face before he set him down. Phainon walked back to where Caelus was standing, waiting for him. “Partner.”

“I’ll make it as painless as possible,” the Trailblazer said, holding his quill up. I…I know from Cyrene…well, your Cyrene, not Demiurge how you two did everything together. Play on the swing, go through oracle cards, run through the wheat fields. Something tells me you’ll find that very person waiting for you at the end of the cosmos. I’ve always wished you two would reunite once again. And now that wish is about to come true.”

Phainon gave him a soft smile, knowing full well what he meant. “I understand. And for what it’s worth, I’m sure she remembers you, Dan Heng and March. She was Mem, after all.”

“That she was.” Caelus quickly turned around to glance at Herta, who was still waiting for them to finish up. “Now I think we should get this show on the road before Madam Herta starts getting impatient. She may be generous unless we don’t waste her time.” He got her attention and she nodded, facing them. Caelus readjusted his grip, poising it upwards. “You ready?”

Of course Phainon was. He had been waiting for this moment for all his life. He dreamt of all the ways they’d meet again–in the wheat fields of Aedes Elysiae under the pale dawn, or in Okhema, or in Janusopolis where she learned more about divination in cycle zero. His first and best friend. The girl who sang lullabies to put him to sleep. The woman who mourned that he had to shoulder the weight of the world they both so deeply loved for so long all by himself.

“I am. Take me to where Cyrene is.”

Caelus smiled. “Close your eyes. Once you feel like your sinking into a deep ocean, transform into your World Bearer state so you can navigate the memoria easily. Remember, time is going to flow differently, so keep that in mind.”

“And we have no idea how long you’ll be there,” added Herta. “But heed my words. Whatever you do, as soon as you enter, do not look back. The space is already a hard place to navigate, so keep moving forward no matter what.

Phainon nodded. “I understand. Cae?”

“On it!” He started to write in the air, a series of Okheman words strung together in gold. “Close your eyes, partner. Madam Herta, a little help please.”

The last thing he saw was Herta pointing her staff at him. A few minutes later he felt a warm gust of air swirling around him, gently tugging his hair and coat tails. It felt nice, like someone was giving him a warm hug on a cold day. It reminded him of the hugs Cyrene gave him whenever he fell and bruised his knees so bad he couldn’t stop the tears. Hah, they way she gently cared for him like a second mother, like a sister…

The other Heirs were right, weren’t they? About him and his emotions. Especially one prince. 

Once Cyrene comes home and they're out of the Exotale, he was going to spend a solid week clinging to her arm like how he did when he was nine. Screw him for feeling emotionally constipated, he just missed his friend so god dang much it hurt.

The wind grew stronger, and stronger, and Phainon felt his feet lift the ground. He heard Caelus muttering something under his breath, accompanied by something swishing downwards. And then–

The Nameless Hero, The Prisoner of Flames found himself plummeting hard towards nothingness.

I wanted to do these two justice and I hope I achieved that! Enjoy reading! The last chapter might come out late but it'll come out soon!

The first thing he saw was endless darkness.

Phainon gasped and opened his eyes, frantically flailing his limbs, trying to gain some semblance of control. Why was it so cold? Why were there no memory fragments of memories scattered about? He thought the sea of memoria would be filled with those. 

Then again, Herta didn’t exactly tell him how the space would look like. The place was blessed by Fuli, and from what he can tell and how he was feeling only followers of the Remembrance had access to the place. Maybe as a sort of protection? The Garden of Recollection did store memories for the Aeon to use after all; having unwanted people that may potentially erase them would be detrimental to their cause.

And then her words hit him like an oncoming wagon that’s in one of Kremnos’ annual races. “Keep moving forward. Whatever you do, do not look back.”

He felt his form shift, the familiar cracks opening on his torso and stomach as his skin turned porcelain white. Gold and onyx wings erupted from his back, and the double halo settled perfectly at the back of his head. If he was going to have any chance of getting out of here safely, he’ll have to be in this form for some time. Not that he had any objections to it. 

Phainon propelled him forward with a single, strong flap and flew with the strong current, using his memories of his childhood to help guide him. The darkness only seemed to grow impossibly darker, like there was a black hole waiting for him at the end of the sea rather than Cyrene. The farther he flew the more the pressure threatened to squish him into a pulp. He had to shut his eyes mid way and let his senses take over and pray that he was going in the right direction. 

How far does the sea flow? The universe was infinite, that much he knew, but it couldn’t be that old, could it? Unless Fuli had decided to have some extra space so it would be convenient for THEM to store memories easily without the extra work. If only THEY thought of organizing the place. Wouldn’t that be nice?

‘Cyrene. Where are you? If only you could give me a sign to help me find you…’ But that was impossible. She was stuck somewhere focusing on keeping Amphoreus’ causality closed. The only thing Phainon could do was use his own memories and use them like how one would use a lamp to illuminate a cave. Maybe that was what Herta wanted him to do?

…The answer seemed to be a little too simple for his liking. What if he was wrong? Or what if it worked but in the wrong way and sends him somewhere entirely different? But it was the only solid plan he had. Based on Herta’s words, this was the logical solution.

Well, fuck.

It was now or never.

And so, he remembered. Phainon started to remember everything. All the good and bad moments he shared with her. The numerous times she made him laugh, the days she held him in her arms when life got hard. Even every time he shoved the Ceremonial Blade into her chest, her golden blood spilling everywhere and tainting the grass and soil. He kept those memories and kept them close to his heart alongside countless others, for they were what kept him going. They were what fueled his very being. His soul.

And now it'd be the torch that'll guide him out of the sea.

He let his body go slack and let it float along with the waves, feeling more confident than before. Now that he knew what he had to do, it was time to let the sea and his mind do the rest. 

And now that his body was getting used to the place, Phainon had to admit it felt nice. Pleasant even. Which was weird for someone like him to say but Fuli was that type of Aeon. The one that welcomed all without any question. It made sense, considering THEY are destined to record everything and ascend once the universe meets its demise. Nothing is left out.

Ok. Maybe some details aren’t that relevant.

Eh, what does he know? 

He travelled farther and farther, and at some point he started to notice a bright light overtaking his vision. He felt his body naturally steer itself towards it, wings angling themselves. The numerous tiny crystals that had been floating idly were now starting to pierce his skin, causing small pinpricks of blood to blotch which healed swiftly. The Coreflames in his body have dwindled considerably, but the effects would linger. 

“Maybe if you had looped the cycles around two million times and stopped it at that we definitely could have extracted everything from your body,” Herta said one day when she came with Caelus to check up on the Heirs. “But the Destruction has run too deep in your body. When you broke from the simulation you became a real person for the time being. Essentially you broke free from your programming and became “real.” So whatever you carried out will stay with you permanently. However, that doesn't mean we can't alleviate the pain. I'll think of something with Screwy and Ruan Mei. They'll have some ideas, especially her.”

At least this power was useful for some things. Like this.

Piercing through something smooth yet sharp. Akin to glass.

Phainon gasped and opened his eyes, realizing what it was–a crystal. 

And its facet showed Aedes Elysiae. 

This had to be the stop! Where else would his dear friend be than the place that was her home. Their home.

Phainon's right arm was halfway through, but the rest of him for some reason refused to cooperate. He grunted as he tried to push through to no avail. He couldn't budge. 

Screaming in frustration he pulled back, flying up until he was at a reasonable height and stared down at the portal. Phainon couldn't give up, not now. He made it all this way. He wasn't about to let some cheap protection trick stop him. The thing was actively rejecting him, most probably because he was an Emanator to Nanook. 

Fuck.

At least he wasn't affiliated with IX. That didn't make his situation any better though.

Fuck.This!

If he has to force himself through with his power, then he will! Fuli isn't here to stop him now, are THEY? One small crack isn't going to be the end of the universe.

So, with a resounding cry, Phainon flew towards the portal as fast he possibly could, letting the remaining Coreflames set his body ablaze. The fire in his heart was burning brighter than before, lit anew with a new purpose. Not to destroy this time, but to save. Cyrene and the others saved his soul and calmed it down while he slumbered. This time, he'd do the rescuing for a change.

‘Please,’ he thought, tears pricking the corner of his eyes as he pushed hard. ‘The cosmos needs her. I need her. She doesn't deserve this fate and you know it! Let me save her! Let me free her!

“LET ME REWRITE THIS STORY ONE. LAST. T̵̢̮̺͇̼̥̪͈͔̹͔̑͜͜I̷̪̱̕M̸͍̦̱̜̠̮̞̤͍̘͝E̵̡͇̱͂́͊̒̄̏̈́̊̆͂̌̄͘̚̚!̶̡̛̝͙͕͗̍̎̀̇̍̑͋̂͌̑

With one last cry, he used whatever strength he had left and pushed and pushed and pushed until white filled his vision and he found himself lying on grass.

Grass?

Oh.

Phainon groaned, standing up on his shaky legs and his breath hitched at the sight in front of him.

Now, one might wonder who would look shell shocked upon seeing their home. It’s their home, and even those who are away from time to time wouldn’t react like they’re seeing it for the first time.But this was different. Because this was the first time Phainon was seeing his home properly, and reuniting with the place after burning it down in every cycle.

Everything looked the same: the mud and cobbled roads, the autumn trees with their orange and yellow leaves, the houses built from stone and love, the pier. There were even two scarecrows meant to represent Caelus, which he thought was funny. The nostalgia was hitting him so hard he thought he was about to fall over again. Cyrene’s memory was always 

Ah.

He just has to wait a few months longer. Soon he’ll be able to stand in the real Aedes Elysiae. And for that to happen…

“Cyrene!” Phainon yelled, jogging down the road. The place was quiet, too quiet for his liking. Well, there was no one here except for her, but there should be signs. He couldn’t find any of those! 

‘Stay calm,’ Phainon kept telling himself. ‘Just because you can’t find anything doesn’t automatically mean the worst has happened. Don’t let your paranoid thoughts get the better of you.’

But where could she have gone?

“Cyrene!?” He yelled again, flitting around the small village. Ugh, if only he could take to the skies! The search would be so much easier. Titans, where was she?? Was she even in Aedes Elysiae? Or was she somewhere in Okhema? How far had this cycle reached? Phainon knows she's immortal but…but…

No. 

Cyrene was strong. She always had been.

And…now that he was thinking properly, there was one place he has yet to check. The place he should have looked in the first place. 

His wings screamed in protest as he made his way towards the swing she always sat on as she stories in her diary to tell to him and the younger children. It was the place they often found themselves lounging around, and Phainon often found himself playing in the water and splashing some onto Cyrene, who’d get all pouty and join him and laugh and laugh and laugh away. God, there were so many memories he had of her over the cycles that focusing on even one was difficult. 

And so, Phainon landed at the wooden dock, nearly stumbled and fell, caught himself, looked up, let the shock consume him at what he saw and promptly ran and hid behind a tree. He took a small peek to make sure his eyes weren’t deceiving him and let out a small gasp.

Because there, sitting near the wooden table, humming the very song she would sing to him to help him sleep was the very woman herself, wearing that beautiful white and purple dress her fourteen year old self always dreamed of owning. Her pink hair was long, the tips dyed turquoise and blue, and even her little elf ears weren't small anymore. On the table was a small bowl of fruit and an open book. A pink and purple quill that looked similar to the one Caelus had lay next to it.

She had a hand resting on her cheek as her eyes flitted back and forth gently, most likely reading her latest entry. The wind chimes tied to the big tree were clinking softly against each other, even though there wasn't a strong enough breeze to even move them. She looked….there wasn't any word to describe the feeling in his heart.

He should move. He had to move, but Khaslana found his legs weren't exactly working. His entire body was in shock by seeing her alive and well and alive. He never saw her as a Goddess. He never saw her as a person who could bend reality on a whim and restore deleted memories to the cosmos. 

No.

He only saw her as his best friend. He only saw her as the girl who he befriended all those years–all those cycles ago. 

And it was this thought that finally made his stubborn legs move. It also must have gotten rid of whatever tiredness was aching his wings, for he stumbled towards her, one food on the ground and the other in the air as he let out what sounded to his ears a desperate cry. 

“Cyrene!!!”

The girl gasped and she spun her around, eyes widening in recognition, but before she could get a word out Phainon practically flew towards her and tackled her into a strong hug and sent them both tumbling to the ground. The table fell over, the beautiful, ripe fruit scattering everywhere, and the chair flew somewhere but he could care less, instead he let the tears he had pent up for so long freely from his eyes. His wings were slumped on the ground, feebly wrapped around their bodies. He took great care not to let his claws scratch her smooth and soft skin. Those hands that ruffled his hair and rubbed soothing circles into his knuckles are on the back of his head and guide it to rest on her chest. That somehow made the tears worse. “Cyrene,” he gasped, swallowing hard. “Cyrene, I–I, I finally–I’m so, so–”

“Shhh,” his best friend said, her fingers scratching his scalp in a way that made his eyes droop. He fought against the urge vehemently. “You’re out of breath, dear Khaslana. You can hear my heartbeat, no? Listen to it and take a deep breath.”

Whatever fear she might have had. Whatever emotions she felt from seeing him, she hid it well right now. In a strange way Phainon felt…almost glad. 

Her calm and kind voice, the slight firmness behind it made Khaslana agree almost instantly. Why wouldn’t he? He listened hard. He listened to the way her heart fluttered. He felt her nose nestle into his hair, the way she muttered words of comfort and told him to calm down. He listened, copying her breathing. It took a while, but soon he didn’t feel like someone was squeezing his lungs and stealing all his hair, but he still didn’t let go. Cyrene made no move to pull back either.

“Phainon?” she whispered, sounding uncertain yet a bit hopeful. “Are you ok?”

Khaslana nodded. “I’m ok…and call me by my birth name. Please.”

Cyrene’s fingers stilled, probably in surprise before chuckling and said in her sweet voice, “Alright then. Khaslana it is.”

Khaslana gasped again, untangling himself from her grasp to look at her face. His fists were curled into fists lying on her chest. Cyrene had a gentle smile on her face, her eyes shining with warmth and mirth, patiently waiting for him to finish whatever inspection he was conducting. In truth he himself had no idea what he was really searching for. Well, except for one.

“Cyrene?” Khaslana asked, his voice small and broken. He felt so horrible for even thinking about the question, and honestly, does it even matter? Does it matter to even ask it, when she still loved him and would love him regardless?

“Fight for this world. This world we both so deeply love.” Those had been her words. Both their words, but she had also said it. So, did it matter?

But then he remembered what Caelus told him about his Cyrene. That she had told stories to the Demiurge and nurtured its heart, letting it blossom into a person–Cyrene herself. The way she envisioned herself if she had grown up. The hard choice she had to make to ensure Amphoreus’-the universe’s survival. The fact he never got a chance to say a proper goodbye…

The words came tumbling out before his brain caught up. “A–are you Cyrene? Or Demiurge? Or–or Mem.”

Cyrene looked a little shocked, eyes searching his face like she was looking for something, understanding what he had just said, and Khaslana spluttered, waving his hands frantically in front of her face. Fuck. Fuck! He knew it was a bad idea to ask. “I’m so sorry! I didn’t mean it like that! I don’t mind who you are now at all!” Titans he was so stupid. If Mydei were here he’d knock him on the head hard. Maybe. Probably. Professor Anaxa would definitely shoot him with his gun.

But then she placed her palm on her mouth and chuckled. It started quiet, then gradually grew louder and louder, until tears formed in her eyes and she was the one now wheezing and out of breath. All Khaslana could do was let out a confused and wounded noise at the sudden outburst. ‘Huh…?’

What…what was so funny?

Khaslana voiced this question and Cyrene merely shook her head, giggling and wordlessly pulled him back into a hug. “Oh my stars!” she gasped after five minutes. “The–there was no need to spew out all those apologies you know? Did you honestly think I’d get offended or mad?”

“I–” Khaslana started to say and promptly shut his mouth. He felt his face heat up in mild embarrassment because she was right. This was Cyrene he was talking to. The girl who always had a smile on her face. The woman who was so strong in her own way and gave strength and hope to those around her. He gulped and chewed his bottom lip, not knowing what to say.

Cyrene chuckled again and pressed their foreheads together. He closed his eyes, letting the touch anchor him. It was something she’d always did before Khaslana had to leave the village to go hunting with the other men or visit the market and buy fresh produce for his mother. “For good luck!” she’d always say, and sometimes she’d even pluck a flower and place it behind his ear. And promptly punched him in the stomach, which led to him punching her arm and then they’d playfight until they were both lying on the ground exhausted for a few minutes.

And…oh.

Oh.

Looks like he got his confirmation after all.

Khaslana didn’t stop the sob that escaped his lips and let the fresh wave of tears pool out as he let the relief wash over him like a tidal wave. It really was her. She was back. And through it all she held him like he was six years old again, like the small boy who dreamt of being a swordsman and fighting against the strongest warriors in Kremnos and ran to Cyrene if something was troubling his heart or if he had hurt himself from self training. Titans, oh Titans he would give everything to turn back time all the way back to cycle zero, back to the Vortex of Genesis where he had to take her life for the very first time. The very first out of 33,550,336 times. If only he could turn back time and urge their younger selves to follow through with their original plans and stay home they could’ve protected all their friends and family.

But, would he? 

Would he really have the guts to do that?

“You know, I can hear you thinking so loudly,” Cyrene giggled softly, pulling away and standing up. Khaslana looked at her confused until she stretched out a hand and said, “Why don’t we go for a small walk down to the pier and have a small chat. I know you have a bunch of questions you want to ask me, and I have some to ask you as well. Plus, sitting down like that for so long will make your legs cramp up, and while you have wings, you still need those too.”

Khaslana blinked, looking down and, sure enough, his legs were bent in a weird angle. Now that she mentioned it, his knees were starting to hurt a bit. Probably because his skin was brittle right now and straining his joints might end up doing irreparable damage to his body. And a walk right now did sound nice. It’s just the two of them right now. It’s been long since it was just the two of them.

So he graciously took her hand and let her haul him up, and he let a mischievous smile grow on his face. Cyrene raised a brow. He snickered and flapped his wings and he was floating off the ground. And then, with the grace of the demigod of World Bearing, he started circling around his best friend playfully, laughing loudly when she groaned. The smile on her face never left as she tried to ‘shove’ him off as she went to grab her journal and quill and even whined out his name. Khaslana merely flew faster, saying her name like how a cheeky younger brother would to his older sister and even booped her on the nose. This was another thing he’d do to her whenever he claimed to have the ‘zoomies’ and would run closely around her endlessly until he got dizzy. She wouldn’t complain, per say, but she’d shoot him a withering glare until he stopped and fall to the floor. A glare she was currently shooting at him now.

Ah.

Some things really do never change.

They made it to the pier without much hassle (Khaslana had to stop after fifteen minutes after his head began to hurt and he feared his halo would get caught with hers) and Cyrene sat down at the edge of the wooden dock, patting the empty spot next to her. Khaslana floated down, letting his wings dip into the water and relishing its coolness. The light from both their halos lit up the river, blending in with the dying sunlight. The whole scene felt…there was no other way to put it, peaceful.

This was the life he had always wanted.

“So,” Cyrene started to say after a while, not looking at him. “How did you get here? The sea of memoria is a volatile place, even for a Lord Ravager.”

Why did you come here? What was happening? was all left unsaid, but Khaslana understood. “I’m here to get you,” he simply said, opting to go straight to the point rather than beat around the bush and tell her the full details. They can wait.

And as he expected that caught her attention and she looked at him in shock and confusion. “Wh–what?” she asked, her voice shaky. 

Khaslana sucked in a breath and reached for her hand. She grabbed it and curled her fingers around his palm. “I know what I’m saying isn’t making much sense. I know you mentally prepared yourself to be here alone forever, to make sure we all live the life you’ve written about for so long. And I kept telling myself how unfair it was. We both started this journey together, and I was the only one that reached the end while you had to become Fuli and hold everything together lest another cosmic war erupts.”

He squeezed her hand. “But Herta–you remember who she is, right?-said we’ve finally got all the materials we needed to reform Amphoreus. Thanks to Caelus, Dan Heng, March and the efforts of the other Nameless we got enough memoria to bring our home into existence. But in order for us to do that, we need someone who has a good grasp on how the power of an Aeon works.”

Khaslana fell silent, letting Cyrene put two and two together and noticed the moment it clicked. “Are–are you–” she closed her eyes to regain composure. “Are you saying that Amphoreus’ causality is about to be sealed permanently? That our home will be born for real?”

“It’s crazy how it only took one year to get everything we need,” Khaslana chuckled. “Even though Herta said it could take anywhere from a few years to a millenia, we all assumed it’d be the latter. But the worst part was…was…”

Khaslana closed his eyes, biting down the overwhelming feeling of sorrow that was overtaking him. He felt Cyrene squeeze his hand, a silent reminder for him to take his time. “The worst part was that I never got a chance to say goodbye,” he choked out. “The only words we exchanged was right before I asked you all to kill me. All we talked about was the mission, and your reassurance that we finally managed to break the cycles. But after that…”

The guilt gnawed at him for days on end after Caelus had told him of her fate. For a total of three days he felt nothing, roaming around the Exotale like a ghost. He felt empty. His best friend was gone. What was supposed to be a victory felt like nothing for him. That was, until a certain prince found him one night sitting at the edge of the Dome and beat some sense into him. He told him words he hadn't wanted to hear at the time. He told him a bunch of stuff that went through one ear and out the other. But looking back…he needed to hear those words. 

After that little ‘pep talk’ he tried to be more active–he snooped in Aglaea's and Anaxa's personal affair with Castorice and Hyacine (though he was the one that got caught and scolded at by them both), he helped Polyxia create new activities each week for the kids, he traded stories with Imperator Cerydra and Hysilens when the three of them sat in front of a bonfire, he dropped in from time to time at the infirmary checking on Hyacine, he, Castorice and Terravox cared for the Chimeras and Dromas babies. Hell he even agreed to steal insane stuff for Cipher and play and hide and seek with Tribbie and her sisters. 

He took Mydei’s advice and threw himself into working so much that, by the time the day was over he was so tired he could hardly stand straight. The best part? He was always so exhausted to the point the nightmares never plague his mind. In fact he didn't have any dreams of the cycles at all!

However, the feeling of regret would always feel heavy in his heart. No matter how hard he distracted himself.

Cyrene flicked her ears, a sad smile on her face. “I never wanted to leave you alone,” she admitted quietly, gripping the fabric of her dress tightly. “Anyone in my position would agree. Khaslana you–You were all alone, carrying a burden very few people would ever bear. I may have never watched you directly killing everyone, but the memories of each cycle as you stab me with the Ceremonial Blade, they fill me with joy and sorrow. Every time I retell the stories to the Demiurge Matrix, I always make sure to include your story. I filled the core with as much love and ego as possible, rewriting the hatred the heart had after being ejected.”

She pointed to her own heart. “Everything that was ever penned in As I've Written is here. Even if Caelus has the book everything will forever be with me. Should the book ever be destroyed or lost to the ages of time, we're all here, forever spreading our story. This was my gift to everyone. To you, Khaslana. You've never reached that one true dawn in any cycle. So, I wanted to make sure you finally did. This was one of my wishes.”

“But how could I enjoy the feeling without you by my side?” Khaslana asked sorrowfully, his wings quivering as his eyes burned. “It felt wrong, so wrong to enjoy the peaceful times while you were looping everything over and over. Leaving you alone was the worst thing I've ever done.”

They fell silent again. Khaslana sniffed and furiously wiped his eyes. The pain he had carried deep within was starting to unravel. Like a ball of yarn he felt himself feeling lighter than he had ever felt in years. What could he say? His family wasn't complete without her. Simple as that.

“I understand,” she finally said. “And I’m sorry for that. No amount of apologizing will undo what I did. I wish I left you a parting gift, or some kind of note, but I know if I did you’d blame yourself for the choice I made. It’s something you can’t help but do, and I don’t blame you one bit. But knowing my true origins…you know I couldn't help but dive in without a second thought.

Khaslana knew what she was talking about. “Does that make you and March siblings?” he teased.

Cyrene laughed. “I suppose so! I've always wished to have a sister, and it looks like that dream came true. Oh, and I think your dream also came true, right?”

“My dream?” Khaslana raised a brow. “To give Amphoreus a bright future?”

“No silly, that's our dream. I mean hooking up with him. The Kremnoan prince you've eyed ever since that trial at the Janusopolis temple in cycle zero?”

“....Oh.” He felt his face heat up. “We've reconciled and sneak into each other’s bed when we think we’re passed out. “We're….slowly getting there.”

“Awwww, you haven't kissed yet?”

“Cyrene!” 

“Ok ok, I'll stop. But I'll say this–love won't be waiting forever you know. You have to seize the opportunity when it presents itself.”

….Why were they talking about his weird situationship/love life right now?

Titans above someone save him from second hand embarrassment. He's so glad she hadn't started asking about wedding plans. He wasn't sure how well he'd be able to handle it.

Cyrene meanwhile was giggling like a teenager who had just walked in on a secret, which was not helping him whatsoever. Ugh, why had he become besties with her?

“You know,” she said after settling down, “it would be nice to finally meet the others properly after so long. I've only written their stories from your observations. It'll be nice to reconnect with them properly. I remember Hyacine promising me that tea party. Castorice also invited me to crochet with her.”

“They all missed you,” Khaslana said. “Even if they've only met you once properly, they felt the weight of your absence.” He let out a soft chuckle. “Aglaea has been meaning to tailor you new outfits she thinks you might fit in. She's made plenty of dresses for us. You're her last victim.”

“Don't say it like it's a bad thing!” Cyrene exclaimed in mock annoyance. “Aglaea's dresses are the prettiest dresses out there. It's not her fault your color sense is atrocious.”

Khaslana balked. “Excuse me!? I'll have you know my fashion sense is absolutely fine! It's not my fault people expect you to dress a certain way with colors they say compliment each other!

They glared at each other, none of them relenting. The only sound that could be heard was from the river and the trees as the wind rustled the leaves. Their halos were glowing harshly, responding to their emotions.

And then…..

“....pfftttttt hahahahha–hic–haahaa!”

Khaslana bent over clutching his stomach as the laughter practically overtook his whole body. His frame was convulsing, wings raised high and he nearly fell back. He could hear Cyrene laughing equally hard, and he was absolutely sure her face was bright red as a tomato. Oh man, his lungs were about to collapse in on themselves at this rate.

If there were still people living here Khaslana had no doubt in mind that the entire village would rush out in panic, wondering who was laughing like a screeching old cat and if Zagreus personally cursed them. Considering Aedes Elysiae is a place protected by Oronyx the Elders would probably be hysterical that the Titan of Trickery managed to cast a spell on one of their own. Good thing it was just the two of them.

“Oh–oh Aeons,” Cyrene choked out, eyes filled with tears. "This is the second time I’ve laughed this hard. You should really heed my advice and become a comedian Khaslana!”

“Of course that’d be the first thing you’d say,” Khaslana groaned. “You and Mydei are the most insufferable people I’ve ever met.”

“But you still love us 🎶.”

“Unfortunately.”

“Hmmm, I don’t think so.”

She stood up and gave him his arm, which he took. Cyrene shot him this excited look and said, “actually, that reminds me. There’s something I want to do before we have to leave. Come with me.”

Khaslana nodded, and that was all the permission she needed and started to lead him towards an arch at the center of the village, painted in dull shades of red, black and white. Flowers lined the perimeter in all sorts of colors, and pots were stacked on the walls.

The Sacrament Courtyard. The temple of Time.

It looked just as he remembered it. A small space nurtured by love and reverence. Ivy curled around the walls, flowers danced in the wind, and the chimes sang for them. It felt like Oronyx was here, at this moment, watching them both. Now that he thought about it, was there an Aeon related to time? Surely it couldn't be Fuli. Terminus perhaps? He'll have to ask Dan Heng later.

The courtyard looked beautiful, yes, but Khaslana suspected that wasn't where she was taking him. They both knew the place by heart after all. No, she was leading them to the space behind the courtyard.

The Oronyx statue.

Cyrene halted once they were standing right in front of it, a cheeky smile on her face as she swiveled on her heel and linked her fingers behind her back. The very same pose she did when she was ‘up to no good.’ Khaslana crossed his arms and raised a question brow. “What? You want to give Them a quick prayer or something?”

“Welllll, now that you've mentioned it, yes!” she chirped. She sat at the edge and pulled out her journal. “But that isn't the main reason dear Khas. Sit down with me, won't you, and indulge in my whims once more?”

Khaslana snorted, muttering under his breath about how they were sitting at the pier for over an hour but complied. His feathers brushed against the statue's base as he folded them behind and brought his legs up to hug them close to his chest. “So then, why are we here?”

“Try to guess,” Cyrene winked, and flipped through the pages of her journal. “While I was here, I did some digging during my free time and wandered the area, searching for some material to write my next story. Honestly I always wondered what our little village hid. I mean, Aedes Elysiae was a place hidden away in the corner of time long before we both started the Recurrences. The story I'm about to tell you now is one I found the very moment I stepped through Time, and sealed off Amphoreus’ causality. It's a story I know you'll understand once I'm done.”

Well, he couldn't deny that her stories were wonderful to hear. With an affirming nod she smiled, closed her eyes, took in a deep breath and started:

Once upon a time, in a small village, relatively unknown to the people outside lived people who worshipped the Time Titan. They were a small group, but they lived in harmony, sharing the produce they grew with everyone and the fish and game they caught from fishing and hunting. They had nothing to fear, for the Titan of Time was watching over them. 

But then, something struck. It wasn't forces from the outside but rather the weather. The rain always graced its presence in this little village. But the villagers noticed slowly how the sun shone relentlessly. They noticed how the crops began to wither and turn to ash, and how the tides were low. Because of this, the forest around them also started to die, and the animals that once inhabited the place fled. 

For a long time, the village was in despair. No one knew what to do, nor what to say. There weren't any other villages nearby to help them. The inhabitants thought they were doomed, and there were talks about relocating. Very few accepted the idea to start anew, but the majority of the citizens were stubborn. They didn’t want to leave behind the life they built that spanned decades. Centuries even. The High Priest, alongside the other Elders turned to Oronyx in a last ditch attempt to save the home they all so dearly loved. The Time Titan did watch over them, though some did question why They would even spend their time in a village tucked away in a place no one would bother checking.

Then, one day a prophecy was received by the High Priest. It was on a normal Wednesday, but that Wednesday changed their lives. He gathered everyone to the statue and told them the prophecy foretold the birth of a child. A special child. And that child would bring forth the rain, and save their dying homeland. They didn’t know when the child would be born, but they all decided to build a courtyard in honor for them. 

And so, they got to work. All the people pitched in, moving bricks, building posts. Even the children helped by preparing their fields for when the rain would pour over the soil and rejuvenate the land. They worked endlessly, with the Elders overseeing the process and offering food and water to everyone everyday. For the first time, a flicker of hope was ignited amongst the people. To outsiders, believing solely on a prophecy was a foolish idea. Prophecies are important, yes, but blindly taking their words seriously? Yet to the people of Aedes Elysiae this prophecy was their salvation. Their final hope. Anyone in their positions would feel desperate. 

Once the building part was done they brought offerings: clay pots, beautiful flowers, food and water, they brought it all. They prayed day and night fervently, hoping that Oronyx would respond. The Time Titan was the youngest of them all, and They always had a soft spot for humanity.

But as the days crawled by, nothing happened. The sun shone as bright as ever, devastating the villagers with its intense heat. The Elders sang songs everyday, urging everyone to not lose their faith. But everyone was convinced Oronyx had abandoned them. Some had even considered cutting their faith to the divine fully. Everyone argued, taking sides. The High Priest tried to take back control and unite the village, but nothing could be done. Soon, he found himself kneeling before the statue at the Temple of Three Fates in Janusopolis, performing rituals with the other priests and priestesses. He and his followers stayed there for a total of 5 days, following the instructions of the Holy Maiden. For five days they worshipped their Titan without fail. The only thing on their mind was Oronyx.

And once the five days were up, they thanked all the priests that helped them and set off for Aedes Elysiae. The journey back was even more arduous but thankfully with the resources they had at their disposal they managed to make it back in one piece. And the moment the High Priest set his foot on the land’s soil–

Rain. Pure rain was falling from the heavens, breathing life slowly into the earth. The party couldn't believe what they were seeing. It was pouring like crazy, and the villagers were running around the muddy roads, laughing in happiness and praising Oronyx for their blessing. A small group who spotted the Priest rushed forward and grabbed all their hands, saying that there was something that they needed to see right away. That there was a miracle waiting for them to witness. The Priest was confused but obliged quickly, for his spirits had been lifted and his heart felt light. The group led them towards the Sacrament Courtyard and to the house next to the Oronyx statue. They knocked on the door softly and led them in. And what they saw would be something they'd never forget.

There, in the middle of the house, sitting on a wooden rocking chair was an old lady, cradling a bundle of blankets. Soft sniffles could be heard, and the lady beckoned the Priest to come forward. And tucked in those blankets was a baby girl with the brightest pink shade of hair and large, cerulean blue eyes with two perfect pink diamonds at the center. Her lashes were long and voluminous as she peered up, and started babbling something. Then, the rain started pouring down faster, as if nature itself understood what she was saying. The Priest was stunned into silence for a few seconds before reaching out to her with his finger, cooing at the little figure when she grabbed it and studied it with interest. “She's real,” the old lady wept. “This child is the one the prophecy foretold would bring Aedes Elysiae back to life.”

The Priest knelt down, unable to tear his eyes away from the baby. “Where did you find her?”

“At the foot of the Oronyx statue, and the moment me and a few other women brought her in, the clouds started to grow dark and lightning filled our vision. It's her, High Priest. She is the one.”

He couldn't deny it. Who would? Aedes Elysiae would live on, and it was all thanks to the bright girl with vibrant pink hair. “We shall have a grand festival in the coming week,” the Priest declared, patting the youngling on the head. The power of Time was strong with her, undeniable. “Those who wish to contribute anything may do so. We shall have a naming ceremony for her at the Sacrament Courtyard.”

“That sounds wonderful,” the old lady said. “But we must decide on a name. She deserves a beautiful one, fit for a Goddess.”

A Goddess? The High Priest hummed in thought. The old lady was right–she deserved to be recognized and worshipped by everyone for generations to come. Of course, he wouldn't want to put all that burden on her once she's all grown up. But coming back to the name….

“Why not name her after our village? This little one saved us all. Why not use half of our village name and bestow that upon her?

“Elysia. The girl who gave us all a second chance. The blessed paradise. That shall be her name.”

Cyrene closed the book and smiled. “That's all! I'll admit, rewriting the whole tale to make it more understanding was a bit of a mental workout. Who would've thought reconstructing a story would be difficult? I mean, you have the whole literature, with extra context. But anyways, how was it? Like it?

Like it?

Khaslana's jaw fell open at that ending. So…so did that mean her existence….her entire existence…. 

But before he could even process her words or even say anything Cyrene got up, pocketed her belongings and held out her hand. “On second thought, how about we save this discussion for later. We've been here for a long time. Who knows how long all our friends have been waiting for us?”

….Oh. Right. He kinda forgot that fact.

Khaslana took her hand and stood up, tilting his head in confusion. “That's true and all, but, uh….what I'm about to ask might be a stupid question, but how exactly are we gonna get out of here? I mean, I'm guessing it's through the sea of memoria, but I'll be honest that place almost ended me. Not physically though.”

“I expected much,” Cyrene replied, winking. “But don't fret! I have an easier way of getting out of here using some Remembrance magic. A little disclaimer before we proceed. It's not…ideal, as some would say, but it is the only other option we have besides swimming through the sea, and it isn't ideal for you. I'll make it as painless as possible, so you don't worry about that. Is that OK for you?”

“Works for me,” Khaslana replied. “What exactly are you gonna do?”

She pulled out her quill and started to write something in the air. “Just wait and watch. Ooh! And close your eyes when I tell you to.” Cyrene started to mutter something under her breath as tiny shards of crystals began to float around them. Khaslana kicked off the ground and started to levitate, trying his absolute best to not flap his wings too much. 

He didn't have to wait too long for her to complete, and once she was done she walked up to him and nodded once. “I'm done setting everything up. Once you give the signal I can transport us back to the present. If you feel uncomfortable at any time, you can squeeze my hand. I can put a small spell on you to help alleviate the worst of the pain, but I'm not sure how long it'll last.”

“That's fine. You've done so much already. I can handle the rest,” Khaslana said, shooting her what he hoped was a reassuring smile. “I'm stronger than you think, heh.”

Cyrene laughed. “Of course you are. I never had any doubts about that.”

“Of course. And, before I give you my confirmation to go ahead with the ritual, there's one small thing I want to say, if you don't mind.”

“Oh? A special message for little old me? Well then, don't keep me waiting! Come on! Say it!”

“Well….all I want to say is…it's an honor to get to know you once again, Elysia of Aedes Elysiae.”

Cyrene fell silent, mirroring his earlier expression when he pieced together the ending of her story. She looked so comical right about now, Phainon wished he had his teleslate on him. The fact he caught Cyrene of all people off guard made him feel giddy. 

Sadly, his victory didn't last for long because Cyrene swiftly bounced back and laughed, grabbing his hand and giving it a quick squeeze. “I wish I told you my real name sooner, back in cycle zero. I'm actually surprised you never knew. Most if not all knew my real name.”

“Excuse me!? When we first met you introduced yourself as Cyrene! How am I supposed to know that's an alias?”

“First off, it's a pen name. And I always introduced myself as Cyrene to everyone!”

“Cyrene, alias' and pen name's are the same thing. But my point still stands! Come to think of it, I don't think my parents ever knew about your real name.”

“Oh, they actually did.”

“...WHAT!??!?”

“They did! They called me by that name a bunch of times, though looking back you were never there for some reason.”

“I feel betrayed,” Khaslana whined, his wings drooping and nearly causing him to fall had Cyrene not caught him in time. “Somehow everyone knew your name was Elysia and I didn’t? I thought we were BFF’S!”

“Well, in your defense I’m certain you weren’t the only one,” Cyrene said reassuringly. “Livia and Piso always called me Cyrene, and never Elysia.”

“Well, those two are airheads after all…”

Cyrene gasped and slapped his arm. “Khas! Be nice!”

“What!? It isn’t like they’re around here!”

“They’re still our friends.”

“Uh, so?”

“Dear Khaslana, do you want me to poke you on the hip right now?”

Khaslana paled. “You wouldn't,” he said nervously, floating back. But Cyrene was wearing that look on her face, and he wasn't taking his chances. “Fine, I won't insult their intelligence further.”

“Good!”

“For now,” he mumbled under his breath. Thankfully she didn't catch that. He took her hand and they both closed their eyes. “I'm ready,” he said out loud. “Go for it, Cyrene. Elysia.”

She hummed, and flashes of purple followed. Before the familiar sinking feeling hit he swore he heard her whisper “we've finally achieved this pale dawn together.” But honestly, that didn't matter.

She was back. That did.

“How do you feel now?”

“Feel?”

“You look much happier now.”

“Do I now….”

Mydei hummed in affirmation, scooting sideways so that their shoulders were almost touching. Phainon's wing automatically found itself resting on his lap. “You were….happy before, but never like this. If I didn't know better, I would've felt jealous.”

“Awwww,” Phainon smirked, reaching over to pinch his prince's cheek. His wings rustled in pleasure at the words. “So you do care about little old me. And here I thought there were no words for affection in the Kremnoan language.”

Said prince scoffed and turned his head away, though he could make out a faint blush dusting his ears. “There aren’t any words for those. That doesn’t mean I don’t care about you, you idiot.” Then, in a low tone, “I’ll always care whether you like it or not.”

Phainon chuckled, hugging him from the back. His fingers skimmed along the deep crimson tattoos, eliciting a shiver from the other. “Such a sap,” he whispered. “Want me to help wash you off?”

“Do what you want.”

Translation: Yes please. Get this grime off of me.

He moved around to grab the soap sitting at the edge of the bath and started to rub his hands across the expanse of back, pressing his thumb against the usual spore spots and massaging them away. It’s a good thing his transformation right now was a partial one, otherwise being near him for this long would be detrimental.

Of course he’d deny the whole pain thing but Khaslana knew better. So what if he still had some of his regenerative healing properties? He promised himself he’d never let anyone get hurt by him ever again.

Mydei sighed in content, closing his eyes. Phainon laughed, his fingers now kneading his shoulders. He really does remind him of a lion lazing around the sun at times like this. “Feels good?” he teased.

“I h–hate to admit it, but it f–fe–feels more than good,” Mydei groaned, slumping against his chest. “But seriously, when were you this good at massaging?”

“Since forever. I’ve done this for my parents since they always toil away at the fields. All you need to know is where the pressure point is at and…press down with just the right amount of force.”

Mydei groaned again, melting into the touch. Phainon snickered under his breath, a wave of amusement and a bit of concern washing over him. He could only wonder why his prince was feeling so many aches everywhere on his body. Could it be because of their constant sparring? No, that doesn’t sound right. Mydei was a strong warrior. A simple workout wouldn’t reduce him to this.

“I can hear you thinking from here,” Mydei grumbled, opening a singular eye and glaring at him. “Speak whatever’s on your mind. You know I’ll always be here to listen.”

Phainon looked at him for a few seconds before sighing, and placed his chin on his shoulder. “Should I be concerned that you’re acting like you’ve just finished carrying a mountain for a whole 6 months. Which, by the way, should be nothing for you.”

Mydei hummed, considering his words. “Under normal circumstances, yes. But even though I die and come back to life, the body still remembers the pain it went through. Every punch. Every kick. Everything is recorded. And then it decides to come back and hit me with the worst chronic pain ever to mankind.”

“I see.” ‘Don’t panic. Keep your calm.’ “Does Hyacine know?”

“She does. I paid her a visit a few weeks ago and she gave me a salve to use for the flareups. The tin is in my room however…”

“Then after we’re done, we’ll head straight there and I’ll help you put the salve on. No buts.”

“Of course you’d say that…” Mydei sighed. He turned to lean against the edge of the tub and opened his arms–a silent invitation, and one Phainon took without any hesitation. He moved to hug him, his wings draping over them both like a huge weighted blanket. Placing his head on his chest he sighed and let his eyes fall shut, and he bit down a weird sound when he felt broad hands stroke his spine, right where the base of his wings would’ve met his back. The area didn’t feel sensitive per say, but it did tickle his brain in a weird way. In a good way?

God does he sound weird right now?

Whatever, the fog in his brain was starting to get heavy.

“Hey,” Mydei gently nudged him. “Don’t fall asleep here. You know better than to lose consciousness while in water.”

“But you’re holding me,” he mumbled, yawning. Seriously, he needed to figure out why his brain was shutting down every single time he felt relaxed. “So I’m in no danger.”

“You trust me that much?”

“Would you ever dare try to drop an Emanator of the Destruction?”

“...So you don’t trust me?”

Phainon sighed and booped his nose. “I was merely joking, Mydeimos. Of course I trust you. Do I need to go through more cycles to prove that?”

Mydei scoffed. “I would prefer you to stay here, with me.” He guided his head back to his chest, right where he could hear his heartbeat. “There’s no need for you to go anywhere anymore. We’re all ok. We don’t need to fight.”

“For now,” Phainon corrected him. “Amphoreus is about to be real in a week. And once that happens…you know what will follow.”

“And we’ll figure it out together. Plus, do you really think the other Heirs would stay silent if Amphoreus is in danger?”

He felt his face heat up, and it had nothing to do with the water. “I–I mean yes, of course they’ll do anything–”

“So stop worrying over everything and nothing. You've got all of us to rely on. Just because you're an Emanator doesn't mean we're weak.”

“Is that…wait no I didn't mean it like that!”

“I know. I'm just making a point.”

Phainon sighed, biting his lower lip. So much for being the best debate champion in every cycle. His words–the one thing he was always good with–are failing him. Funny how out of all the Heirs he was the most chattiest one, and right now his brain was scrambled, trying to string together sentences that made sense. “Fuck this,” he muttered at last, squeezing his eyes short. “I hate this feeling.”

“Feeling?” Mydei parroted.

“Feeling helpless. Sometimes I feel like I don’t have control of my own body. I want to do things, try new stuff out and rediscover my passion for the hobbies I used to indulge in. But doing anything these days has me feeling exhausted out of my mind. I try to focus on something and my mind is just….drifting away.”

Honestly that was the best way he could describe his predicament without using complicated, fancy words. He might go visit Anaxa and try some stimulation exercise to get his fingers to work right again. Oh, and figure out which activities could help with his brain. 

And speaking of his fingers… “They feel lighter now all of a sudden.”

Mydei made a questioning noise. “Hm?”

“My fingers. Ever since rescuing Cyrene they've been feeling a lot less dense. At first it felt like I was carrying something really heavy. Almost like the weight of the world and…and my sins.” He winced when the word left his mouth. “But after sitting down at the pier and having that talk with her, I feel better. Not completely better, but it feels like I will get better in the foreseeable future.”

And he found he meant it. The burden that had been weighing his heart was still there, but it wasn't actively trying to smother him. Instead it was lying low, staying quiet. It was going to be there for a long time as a silent reminder he couldn't forget nor escape, but he could learn to accept and live alongside it.

Perhaps that would be the best outcome for everyone.

Mydei’s breathing hitched, and calloused fingers placed themselves under Phainon's chin and lifted his head up. Those beautiful sunset eyes looked at him with such fondness he felt his heart ache from it all. The sheer love and adoration from his partner, knowing he–and everyone else–accepted and wanted to help him.

Fuck.

He felt his eyes water.

And Mydei immediately looked concerned as his thumbs worked to wipe them as quickly as they came. “Phainon? What happened?”

“Nothing,” he choked out, broken laughter spilling from his lips as the tears started to blur his vision. “I just, I just don't know what to do with all this love Mydei. I'm so used to giving it freely. Being on the receiving end feels so weird. I'm worried I'll crumble under the weight of it all.”

The old him would've added that he'd gladly perish. His duty to his world was over. Why does he need to walk on its soil?

Mydei huffed a laugh, hugging him tightly once more, fingers brushing against his feathers. “And that's why we're here. Let us be the mold that will keep you together. We'll be here for you no matter what. You have all of us Phainon. You have me. So use our strength to heal yourself. You’re not a leech, you need support and we want you to accept it. There’s a difference, and you know it.”

You aren’t a leech. You need support. We want to give it to you.

Why did he feel like he had to hear those words?

Maybe because he was right. Maybe because his heart was waiting for someone to say those words out loud for some time. 

It was hard. Things never got easier but when have things ever been easy? During every hardship the Heirs had each other for support, and yes that also included Professor Anaxa. If they felt all hope was lost they could message whom they wanted to and the person would show up without hesitation. 

So then, why should things be any different now? The feeling stirring in his heart was nothing he wasn't used to. Armed with the knowledge of thirty three million cycles, Phainon was hesitant to live a normal life, but now…

Now, he wasn't the only person. The only thing he still had was the combined heat of all the Coreflames. But that wasn't physically and mentally stopping him from looking at his partner, who had a patient look on his face, waiting for his reply.

You guys haven’t kissed yet?

Well, it was high time he changed that.

And so Phainon wiped his tears from his eyes, ignoring the small cracks that started to form on his face, looped his arms around his neck and yanked him down to press his lips to his.

It wasn’t deep, it wasn’t rushed, just slow and full of passion and love. And oh he had to admit he did miss this. Titans, why was Cyrene always right about him? Especially about the part where love suits him and he should embrace it without worry? But how could he not worry? After all, every single person he loved dearly died by his own hands. Their golden blood stained his weapons and fingers. How could he love freely? Moreover, how could they care about him?

But then he felt a finger trace his jaw before cupping it and tilting his head ever so slightly and suddenly it all clicked into place. Love was never conditional. Love didn't mean choosing certain people and throwing affection at them. Love never meant shunning out those who believe they deserve nothing but hatred.

Everyone loves each other in their different ways, and that's why relationships are always complicated but beautiful. Aglaea, before her humanity was stripped, had loved her creations, and the people she would come to later protect. Cipher may have been a greedy thief, but she still cared for the people that lived in poverty and checked on her mother figure from time to time. Mydei’s love was a tad bit different–he still loved war like the other Kremnoans, but he always did his best to avoid it at all cost, and always took each blade to shield his people, and his five most dearest friends. 

Ah.

That was the beauty of love.

They parted and Mydei chuckled, kissing his forehead and his mouth once more and said, “how do you feel after doing that? Comfortable?” 

There was a bit of hesitancy in his voice, so Phainon quickly dissipated those thoughts by kissing his cheek and smiling brightly. “If I wasn’t ready, I wouldn’t have initiated it, right?”

“Of course, but I’m just making sure here.”

“Oh, Mydei. I don’t think I’ve ever been so sure of something in my life.” And they kissed again, and again until they were both almost fully submerged in the water and–

“Looks like someone has finally taken my advice.”

Phainon's eyes blew wide open as he pushed back harshly, ignoring how Mydei groaned as he rubbed his aching nose. His head slowly turned, hoping that if he moved slowly the person on the other side would somehow disappear. 

She in fact, did not disappear.

Cyrene was standing right there with her arms folded and a smirk tugging at her lips. She was dressed in a pretty pale pink and white swimming suit with her hair tied up in a ponytail. Upon seeing her attire though, Phainon froze like a deer on headlights.

Oh shit. 

How did he forget she was going to join them today in the baths!? And now she witnessed them making out. A bit too passionately if he may add.

He looked at Mydei, who looked like he was cycling between five different emotions at the same time. His ears weren't a bright red as he trudged over and whispered furiously into his ear. “You didn’t tell me Cyrene would be coming over!”

“It–it somehow slipped my mind!” Phainon shot back, equally embarrassed. Oh, there was no escaping her teasing now.

Cyrene laughed, stepping closer and crouching at the edge of the bath. “Don't worry, I didn't click any photos for black mail material if that's what you're wondering. But I do wish I had captured something!” she squealed at the end. “You see Phai? You are capable of loving others! You just have to trust yourself.”

Phainon sighed, stepping back to let her settle down. “Yeah yeah,” he softly admitted.  “You were right. As always.”

“As always?” Mydei snorted, who had regained his composure at some point.

He shrugged. “I told you she was a diviner. And she was the calmer one between the two of us soooo–”

“So I had to keep divining to make sure you didn’t end up in any trouble. Since I was the calmer one, that gave you permission to act recklessly as you please, didn’t it?” 

Phainon sputtered, pointing a finger at her and babbling something while Mydei was roaring with laughter now, head tilted all the way back. Cyrene had a hand over her mouth, stifling her own giggles. How wonderful, he was now the laughingstock.

Fuck it.

At least it was just the two of them. 

Chapter End Notes

I'll see you in the next one!
